headline: A windy, rainy front hits Friday, then a stronger windy round Saturday night, with an active, stormy pattern continuing into next week.
summary: As of Thursday evening, a strong front from the Pacific brings rain starting tonight and spreading across western Washington early Friday morning, with gusty winds. The windiest spots are the coast, the Whidbey and San Juan Islands, and the northern interior (including western Whatcom and Skagit counties), where winds of 20-30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph are possible. Wind Advisories are in effect there on Friday: 1 AM to 1 PM for the Northern Washington Coast, 4 AM to 4 PM for Island County, the western Skagit and northwestern Snohomish lowlands, the western Whatcom lowlands and San Juan County, and 7 AM to 4 PM for the Grays Harbor County Coast. Most of the rain falls during the day Friday, about one-half to three-quarters of an inch at most over the higher terrain and coast, and one-tenth to one-quarter of an inch in most other lowland areas. Snow levels are high, starting around 5,000-6,000 feet and rising to about 9,000 feet in the afternoon, so high-elevation snow is not a big concern. Saturday is a relative lull, with leftover clouds, some showers and highs in the 60s in most lowlands. Another front arrives Saturday night with a new round of strong winds. The coast, islands and northern interior will likely see advisory-level winds, and other places along Puget Sound could too, but it is too early to decide on alerts. Winds ease quickly Sunday, with most breezy conditions ending by mid-morning. After a brief break Sunday night into Monday, more rain comes Monday afternoon into Tuesday. Temperatures stay a few degrees above normal, with lows mostly in the mid 40s to around 50. Forecasters are fairly confident about Friday's winds because computer models have been consistent. Which areas get strong winds Saturday night is less certain, and Wednesday is low confidence because models disagree on whether rain reaches at least the Olympic Peninsula. No river flooding is expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will soak the ground and raise river flows, which could matter with later storms next week. Rough seas and gale conditions are in place on the coastal and northern waters, and rough to severe conditions are possible on the Grays Harbor Bar starting Friday.
changes: The morning discussion mentioned a large swell and 20-foot seas, while later ones focused more on Saturday night's wind, with more detail on which areas could see strong winds. Later updates also added a brief break Sunday night into Monday, then rain Monday afternoon into Tuesday, and flagged model disagreement about Wednesday.
